sources.entry: MeiliSearch - Ultra relevant, instant and typo-tolerant full-text search API. (Source Code) MIT Rust/Docker/deb

summary.one_liner: Meilisearch is an open-source, MIT-licensed search engine that provides a fast, typo-tolerant full-text, semantic, and hybrid search API, available as a managed cloud service or self-hosted.
summary.what_it_does:
Meilisearch is a search engine exposing a RESTful API for full-text, semantic, and hybrid search. The README describes typo tolerance, search-as-you-type with results under 50 ms, filtering and faceted search, sorting, synonyms, and geosearch. It also covers API keys with fine-grained permissions, tenant tokens for multi-tenancy, search rules, document relations, and extensive language support including Chinese, Japanese, and Hebrew. AI-related features include conversational search, a native MCP server at /mcp (marked experimental), a LangChain vector store integration, and an llms.txt docs index. Enterprise Edition adds sharding, replication, S3-streaming snapshots, and search rule previews under a commercial or Business Source License 1.1 arrangement. The README also offers a managed Meilisearch Cloud service as the recommended option.</what_it_does>

use_cases: add full-text search to a website or app
self-host a search backend with Docker
build a faceted ecommerce product search
hybrid or semantic search over documents
give AI agents search access via MCP or LangChain
typo-tolerant search for movies or catalogs
how_to_run: curl -L <install-url> | sh (URL not preserved in README text)
Add documents with a POST request to the documents endpoint using a Bearer API key
Search with a POST request whose JSON body contains a q field
Install a language SDK (JavaScript, Python, PHP, Ruby, Go, Rust, or React quick starts are listed)
notable: Typo-tolerant full-text plus semantic and hybrid search in one engine
Single-binary or Docker self-hosting with the same API as the managed cloud
Fine-grained API keys and tenant tokens for multi-tenant apps
Native MCP server and LangChain vector store for AI agent use
Community Edition under MIT; Enterprise features under a separate commercial license
caveats: Enterprise Edition features such as sharding and S3 snapshots are not allowed in production without a commercial agreement
The MCP server is marked experimental
The README recommends Meilisearch Cloud, which is a paid managed service after a 14-day trial
Indexing is asynchronous, so new documents may not appear in search immediately
